title: Canonical item matching
lead: Map parsed item text to canonical grocery items with categories and aliases (I6).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the review UI (next slice); order-line matching (Phase 2 reuses this).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: "ground turkey meat" and "ground turkey" must be the same thing on the list. Order lines in Phase 2 will reuse the same matcher.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
None beyond ADR 0019.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-04, ADR 0019 (S15): no staples are seeded (the household adds them); category order is produce, meat, dairy, bakery, canned, dry goods, spices, frozen, household, pet.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-04, ADR 0019 amended (S16): the unit table is Python constants in src/larder/ingredients/units.py; S17 seeds the unit and unit_alias rows from it.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-04, answered in the spec check: (1) the seed is an idempotent insert-missing step at startup beside db.migrate and sync_people; it only inserts missing items, categories by name, aliases and unit rows and never updates or deletes existing rows; (2) ingredient_line.confidence stores the lower of the parse confidence and the match confidence, a line is flagged below the existing REVIEW_THRESHOLD of 0.8, and item_id is set to the best candidate when one exists (NULL only when there is no token overlap); (3) S17 ships a callable such as parse_and_match_recipe(conn, recipe_id) and its writer, and S18's 're-apply during indexing' step wires it into the S13 index flow; S13 is not a dependency of S17.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Seed items, categories and aliases from TOML (ADR 0019).
2. Normalize: lowercase, strip descriptors (fresh, chopped, sliced, …), and singularize with simple rules.
3. Match on exact, then alias, then token overlap (stdlib `difflib` for the score).
4. Return the item with a confidence; below the threshold → review queue.
5. Store the whole parse from S16's `ParsedLine` on `ingredient_line` (qty, qty_max, unit_id, item_id, notes, optional, is_food, confidence), and the extra choices in `ingredient_line_alt` (S59). This slice is the only writer of parsed fields; S13 writes raw lines and S16 stays pure.

Spec-check note from S16 review (2026-11-04): src/larder/ingredients/units.py has no dimension per unit, but the unit table's dimension column is NOT NULL with the values mass, volume, count and package (migration 0001). Add a canonical-unit-to-dimension map next to UNIT_SYNONYMS before seeding the unit table: clove is a count; can and jar are packages (PACKAGE_UNITS); tbsp, tsp, cup, ml and l are volume; lb, oz, g and kg are mass.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - Matching tests pass; all fixture ingredients map or are queued.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Add canonical item matching with seeded items and aliases (S17).
